source_text: Quonram autem quidam ex his qui putantur recte credidisse, supergrediuntur ordinem promotionis justorum, et modos meditationis ad incorruptelam ignorant, hzereticos sensus in se habentes: heeretici enim despicientes plasmationem Dei, et non suscipientes salutem carnis suze, contemnentes autem et repromissionem Dei, et totum supergredientes Deum sensu, simul atque mortui fuerint, dicunt se supergredi ccelos et Demiurgum, et ire ad matrem, vel ad eum qui ab ipsis affingitur, patrem. Qui ergo universam reprobant resurrectionem, et quantum in ipsis est auferunt eam de medio, quid mirum est, si nec ordinem resurrectionis sciunt, nointelligere, quoniam si heec ita essent, quemadmodum dicunt, ipse utique Dominus, in quem se dicunt credere, non in tertia die fecisset resurrectionem; sed super crucem exspirans, confestim utique abiisset sursum, relinquens corpus terre? Nemo enim est discipulus super magistrum : perfectus autem omnis, erit | sicut magister ejus. Quomodo ergo magister noster non statim evolans abiit, sed sustinens definitum a Patre resurrectionis suze tempus, quod et per Jonam manifestatum est, post triduum resurgens assumtus est; sic et nos sustinere debemus definitum a Deo resurrectionis nostree tempus, preenuntiatum a prophetis, et sic resurgentes assumi, quotquot Dominus ad hoc dignos habuerit*,
pass_a_gloss: For certain of those who are thought to have believed correctly, nevertheless transgress the order of the promotion of the just, and the modes of meditation to incorruptibility, having heretical senses in themselves: for heretics, despising the creation of God, and not receiving the salvation of their own flesh, but also despising the promise of God, and transgressing the whole sense of God, as soon as they have died, say that they will transgress the heavens and the Demiurge, and go to the mother, or to him who is affixed by them, the father. Who therefore reject the whole resurrection, and as far as it is in their power, take it away from the midst, what wonder is it, if they do not know the order of the resurrection, nor understand, since if these things were as they say, the Lord himself, in whom they say they believe, would not have made the resurrection on the third day; but having expired on the cross, would have gone up immediately, leaving the body to the earth? But now, having conversed for three days where the dead were, as the prophet says of him: The Lord is mindful of his holy ones, who have slept in the earth of burial, and he descended to them, to draw them out and save them. And the Lord himself says: As Jonas was in the belly of the whale for three days and three nights, so will the Son of Man be in the earth. But also the Apostle says: He ascended, what is it, if not that he also descended into the lower parts of the earth? And David, prophesying about him, said: You have delivered my soul from the lowest hell. But rising again on the third day, and Mary, who first saw him, adored, saying: Do not touch me, for I have not yet ascended to the Father, but go to the disciples and say to them: I ascend to my Father and your Father. If therefore the Lord observed the law of the dead, that he might become the firstborn from the dead, and having remained until the third day among the dead of the earth, afterwards rising in the flesh, that he might also show the marks of the nails to the disciples, thus he ascended to the Father, how are they not confounded, who say that the lower world is indeed this world, which is according to us; but the inner man of theirs, leaving the body here, ascends to a super-celestial place? For when the Lord went away in the midst of the shadow of death, where the souls of the dead were, afterwards he rose again bodily, and after the resurrection he was taken up: it is manifest that also the souls of his disciples, for whom the Lord also worked these things, will go to an invisible place, defined for them by God, and there they will remain until the resurrection, sustaining the resurrection: afterwards receiving their bodies, and rising again perfectly, that is, bodily, just as the Lord rose again, thus they will come to the sight of God. For no one is a disciple above his master: but every perfect one will be like his master. How therefore did our master not immediately fly away, but sustaining the defined time of his resurrection by the Father, which was also manifested through Jonas, rising again after the three days, was taken up; so also we ought to sustain the defined time of our resurrection by God, preannounced by the prophets, and thus rising again, be taken up, as many as the Lord will have deemed worthy.

pass_b_english: Certain people who are thought to have believed correctly nevertheless transgress the order of the advancement of the just and remain ignorant of the modes of meditation that lead to incorruptibility, for they harbor heretical sensibilities within themselves. Indeed, heretics despise God's creation and refuse to receive the salvation of their own flesh; they also despise God's promise and transcend the whole sense of God, so that as soon as they die they claim they will transcend the heavens and the Demiurge and go to the mother, or to the one they fabricate as the father. Since they reject the entire resurrection and, as far as it lies in their power, remove it from the midst, what wonder is it that they do not know the order of the resurrection nor understand it? For if things were as they say, the Lord himself, in whom they claim to believe, would not have accomplished the resurrection on the third day; instead, having breathed his last on the cross, he would have gone up immediately, leaving his body to the earth.

But as it is, he remained for three days where the dead were, just as the prophet says of him: "The Lord is mindful of his holy ones, who have slept in the earth of burial, and he descended to them, to draw them out and save them" (Psalms 16:10). The Lord himself also says: "As Jonah was in the belly of the whale for three days and three nights, so will the Son of Man be in the heart of the earth" (Jonah 1:17). The Apostle likewise says: "He ascended—what does this mean except that he also descended into the lower parts of the earth?" And David, prophesying concerning him, said: "You have delivered my soul from the lowest hell." Rising again on the third day, and when Mary, who saw him first, adored him, he said to her: "Do not hold on to me, for I have not yet ascended to the Father; but go to the disciples and say to them: I am ascending to my Father and your Father" (John 20:17).

If therefore the Lord observed the law of the dead so that he might become the firstborn from the dead, and having remained until the third day among the dead of the earth, he afterwards rose in the flesh in order to show the disciples the marks of the nails, and thus ascended to the Father, how are they not confounded who say that the lower world is this world, which belongs to us, while their inner man, leaving this body behind, ascends to a super-celestial place? For when the Lord departed into the midst of the shadow of death, where the souls of the dead were, he afterwards rose bodily, and after the resurrection he was taken up. It is therefore manifest that the souls of his disciples also, for whose sake the Lord accomplished these things, will go to an invisible place appointed for them by God, and there they will remain until the resurrection, awaiting the resurrection; afterwards, receiving their bodies and rising perfectly—that is, bodily, just as the Lord rose—they will come into the sight of God. For no disciple is above his master; but everyone who is perfected will be like his master. How, then, did our master not immediately fly away, but waited for the appointed time of his resurrection defined by the Father, which was also manifested through Jonah, and rising after three days was taken up? So also we ought to wait for the appointed time of our resurrection defined by God, preannounced by the prophets, and thus rising be taken up, as many as the Lord will have deemed worthy.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text, including the complex theological distinctions regarding the heretical view of the 'inner man' versus the 'body'. Scripture citations in Pass B (Psalms 16:10, Jonah 1:17, John 20:17) correctly identify the biblical sources alluded to in the Latin text. The title 'Resurrection and the Heretics' appropriately names the thought of the chapter.
